title: 第四章 哥伦布的好日子

outline.title: 一个正在生成的周年纪念日
卡斯蒂利亚人与扬基佬

children: I walked past Vasco da Gama’s body with premonitions of typhoons. I was in Portugal, at the Mosteiro dos Jéronimos, right where Europe started to redefine the world. Here Lisbon becomes Belém, in honor of Bethlehem, to absorb in the memory of the West the Orient where Christ was born. Here Da Gama knelt for his last blessing before facing the seven seas. Here he was brought back to be buried as if to engrave on this soil the history of uncharted oceans.

我走过瓦斯科·达伽马（Vasco da Gama）的遗体，心中掠过台风将至的预感。我身在葡萄牙，在热罗尼莫斯修道院（Mosteiro dos Jéronimos），就在欧洲开始重新定义世界的地方。在这里，里斯本变成了贝伦（Belém），以纪念伯利恒（Bethlehem），把基督诞生的东方吸纳进西方的记忆。在这里，达伽马在直面七海之前跪下领受最后的祝福。在这里，他被运回安葬，仿佛要把未经测绘的大洋的历史铭刻在这片土地上。

There were too many facts for that story to be simple—too many names crowding my thoughts, too many relics for a single image. This monastery was named after one Saint Jerome whose Hieronymite followers ran plantations in Santo Domingo. Its monstrance was made with gold that Da Gama, en route to Calicut, extorted from the Muslim sultan of Kilwa. Its main entrance faced an avenue called India. Everything here evoked an elsewhere and the hidden face of Europe: Christendom had not left a single continent untouched. The world started and ended here with a confusion of tongues and cultures.

对那个故事来说，事实太多了，多到无法简单——太多名字挤满我的思绪，太多遗物无法凝成单一的形象。这座修道院以某位圣热罗尼莫（Saint Jerome）命名，他的热罗尼莫会（Hieronymite）追随者曾在圣多明各经营种植园。它的圣体光座是用达伽马在前往卡利卡特（Calicut）途中从基尔瓦（Kilwa）的穆斯林苏丹那里勒索来的黄金打造的。它的正门对着一条名叫印度的大道。这里的一切都唤起某个别处，唤起欧洲隐藏的面孔：基督教世界没有放过任何一块大陆。世界在这里开始，也在这里结束，伴随着语言与文化的混淆。

The babel of Belém intruded on my memories: Jerome, Jéronimos, Hieronymites. Had not that name become a symbol of native resistance in the United States after an Indian born Goyahkla, in what used to be Mexico, was renamed Geronimo? My feelings as jumbled as the lands of Arizona, I kept wondering why so many Europeans deny that they created the United States. Didn’t the line go straight from Afonso de Albuquerque to Albuquerque, New Mexico? Had not Da Gama died in Cochin less than five hundred years before Vietnam?

贝伦的巴别喧嚣闯入我的记忆：热罗尼莫（Jerome）、热罗尼莫斯（Jéronimos）、热罗尼莫会士（Hieronymites）。一个出生在一片曾属于墨西哥的土地上、本名戈亚克拉（Goyahkla）的印第安人被改名为杰罗尼莫（Geronimo）之后，这个名字难道不是在美国成了原住民抵抗的象征吗？我的心绪如亚利桑那的土地一样杂乱，我不停地想：为什么那么多欧洲人否认他们创造了美国？那条线难道不是从阿方索·德·阿尔布开克（Afonso de Albuquerque）笔直连到新墨西哥州的阿尔伯克基（Albuquerque）吗？达伽马死在科钦（Cochin），距越南战争难道不足五百年吗？

Outside the monastery, the sun over Belém spoke of pasts unknown and uncertain waters. I turned away from the Jéronimos. On the Avenue of Brazil, Lisbon flaunted further its long encounter with the seas. Yet the surfeit of names continued to defy the established story. There were too many signs here for history to remain official. Images of India, of Indians north, south, and west—from Calicut to Brazil, from Brazil to Arizona, persistent flavors of continents conquered in the name of spices and gold filled up the empty space between the monuments.
修道院外，贝伦上空的太阳诉说着不为人知的过去和吉凶未卜的水域。我转身离开热罗尼莫斯修道院。在巴西大道上，里斯本进一步炫耀它与海洋的漫长相遇。然而，繁多的名字却仍冲撞着既定的故事。这里的记号太多了，历史无法保持官方版本。印度的形象，北方、南方、西方的印第安人（Indians）的形象——从卡利卡特到巴西，从巴西到亚利桑那，以香料和黄金之名被征服的各大洲挥之不去的气息，填满了纪念碑之间的空白。

Moving among these ghosts, I savored the irony of this human landscape caught in the wheels of time. A clutter of colonial paraphernalia displayed itself on and off an avenue called Brazil—after the colony that for a brief moment was Portugal’s metropolis. On my right, overlooking the Tagus, the Tower of Belém reminded me of piracy, of the time when Europe had to defend itself against its own. On my left, a few hundred yards from the Tower, the Monument to the Discoveries repackaged Portugal’s past in a grandiose display of adventurous innocence.

在这些幽灵之间穿行，我品味着这幅被时间之轮碾住的人文景观的反讽。名叫巴西的大道内外，摆满了形形色色的殖民时代遗物——这条大道的名字来自那个曾短暂成为葡萄牙本国统治中心的那个殖民地。在我的右侧，俯瞰特茹河（Tagus）的贝伦塔（Tower of Belém）让我想起海盗，想起欧洲不得不防备自己人的年代。在我的左侧，距贝伦塔几百码处，发现者纪念碑（Monument to the Discoveries）以一场宏大的、天真无邪的冒险展演，重新包装了葡萄牙的过去。

A tribute to Prince Henry the Navigator, whose quincentennial it honored in 1960, the huge structure shows the Prince leading the Portuguese to the Discoveries. But the memorial was just too big to convince me of its chastity: its arched mass spoke of conquest, of Henry’s desire to bend the onlooker under his will. Here Bethlehem met Brazil. Here Europe was confused about where it came from and where it had taken the world. Here anyone was at home and yet no one could rest in peace—not even Da Gama, whose remains were bought by the Portuguese in exchange for their weight in gold.

这座巨大建筑是对航海家恩里克王子（Prince Henry the Navigator）的致敬——1960年正值他去世五百周年——它展示王子率领葡萄牙人奔向大发现。可是这座纪念碑实在太大了，大到让我没法相信它真的那样清白：它拱形的体量诉说着征服，诉说着恩里克要把观者压服在自己意志之下的欲望。在这里，伯利恒遇上了巴西。在这里，欧洲弄不清自己从何而来，又把世界带往了何方。在这里，任何人都如归故里，却没有人能安息——连达伽马也不能，他的遗骸是葡萄牙人用等重的黄金买回来的。

In the few square miles of Belém, the managers of history had tried repeatedly to impose a narrative. Perhaps they had tried too much. For in the monumental efforts of the Portuguese state to catch up with a history now eclipsed by nostalgia, I saw the nostalgia of the entire West for a history that it never lived, its constant longing for a place that exists only in its mind. The West was Calicut, Brazil, Cochin and Kilwa. The West was America, a dream of conquest and rapture. In the confusion of Belém, I could almost hear this line from Mon Oncle d’Amérique: “America does not exist. I know. I’ve been there.”

在贝伦这区区几平方英里内，历史的经营者们一再试图强加一套叙述。也许他们用力过猛。因为在葡萄牙国家为追赶一段如今已被怀旧遮蔽的历史而做的宏大努力中，我看到的是整个西方对一段它从未经历过的历史的怀旧，是它对一个只存在于其头脑中的地方的不断渴望。西方就是卡利卡特、巴西、科钦和基尔瓦。西方就是美洲，一个征服与狂喜之梦。在贝伦的混乱中，我几乎能听到《我的美国舅舅》（Mon Oncle d’Amérique）里的这句台词：“美洲并不存在。我知道。我去过那里。”

Except that I was in Belém whence Europe’s face looked no clearer than that of the Americas, no truer than that of Prince Henry, of whom there is no surviving picture. The Monument to the Discoveries had to invent a face for the Prince, just as Europe had to invent a face for the West. Belém’s steady effort to patch up its own silences did not reflect on Portugal alone. It spoke of the entire West—of Spain, France, and the Netherlands, of Britain, Italy, and the United States—of all those who, like Columbus, had come from behind to displace Portugal in the reshaping of the world. And as much as I did not like it, as much as Prince Henry might disagree, it spoke also of me, of all the lands disturbed by their cacophony. Jerome, Jéronimos, Hieronymites—was anyone left untouched?

只是我身在贝伦，从这里望去，欧洲的面孔并不比美洲的面孔更清晰，也不比恩里克王子的面孔更真实——后者没有任何画像传世。发现者纪念碑不得不为王子发明一张脸，正如欧洲不得不为西方发明一张脸。贝伦不断修补自身沉默的努力，反映的不只是葡萄牙。它诉说着整个西方——西班牙、法国和荷兰，英国、意大利和美国——诉说着所有那些像哥伦布一样后来居上、在重塑世界的过程中取代葡萄牙的人。而且，尽管我不喜欢这样，尽管恩里克王子可能不同意，它也诉说着我，诉说着所有被这片刺耳喧嚣搅扰的土地。热罗尼莫、热罗尼莫斯、热罗尼莫会士——还有谁未被触动？

In 1549, soon after the Hieronymites started their plantations on Haitian soil, the Franciscans began their mission in Japan. I went back to my hotel, thinking of Columbus who once thought also that he had reached Japan. I could now glimpse the truth of my own history: The West does not exist. I know. I’ve been there.
1549年，就在热罗尼莫会士在海地土地上开办种植园后不久，方济各会开始了他们在日本的传教。我回到旅馆，想着哥伦布——他也曾一度以为自己到达了日本。我如今得以窥见我自己历史的真相：西方并不存在。我知道。我去过那里。

body.review: 底本作 Franciscans（方济各会）。1549年抵达鹿儿岛的传教团由耶稣会士方济各·沙勿略率领。

en: October 12, 1492

History is messy for the people who must live it. For those within the shaky boundaries of Roman Christendom, the most important event of the year 1492 nearly happened in 1491. Late at night on November 25, 1491, Abu l-Qasim al-Muhli signed the treaties by which the Muslim kingdom of Granada surrendered to the Catholic kingdom of Castile, ending a war the issue of which had become clear a few months earlier. The transfer of power was scheduled for May, but some of the Muslim leaders decided not to wait for the Christian takeover and left town unexpectedly. Granada’s Nasrid ruler, Muhammad XII Boabdil, rushed the capitulation. Thus, it was almost by accident that the flag of Castile and the cross of Christendom were raised over the tower of the Alhambra on January 2, 1492, rather than during the previous fall, as first expected, or the following spring, as scheduled.
zh: 对于必须身在其中过活的人来说，历史是杂乱的。对罗马基督教世界摇摇欲坠的边界之内的人而言，1492年最重要的事件差点发生在1491年。1491年11月25日深夜，阿布·卡西姆·穆赫利（Abu l-Qasim al-Muhli）签署了穆斯林格拉纳达王国向天主教的卡斯蒂利亚王国投降的条约，结束了一场胜负在几个月前就已明朗的战争。权力移交原定于五月，但一些穆斯林领袖决定不等基督徒接管，出人意料地离开了城。格拉纳达的纳斯里德王朝统治者穆罕默德十二世博阿布迪尔（Muhammad XII Boabdil）仓促促成了投降。于是，几乎出于偶然，卡斯蒂利亚的旗帜和基督教世界的十字在1492年1月2日升上了阿尔罕布拉宫（Alhambra）的塔楼，而不是像最初预期的那样在前一年秋天，或像日程安排的那样在次年春天。

en: For actors and witnesses alike, the end of the

was a disorderly series of occurrences, neither a single event, nor a single date. The end of the war and the signing of the treaties—both of which occurred in year 1491 of the Christian calendar—were as significant as the flight of the Muslim leaders, the raising of the Christian flag, or the glorious entry of the Catholic monarchs into the conquered city on January 6, 1492. The capitulation of Granada was, however, as close to a milestone as history in the making can get. Milestones are always set in regard to a past, and the past that Western Christendom had fashioned for itself projected the moving Spanish frontier as the southernmost rampart of the cross.
zh: 对行动者和见证者而言，

的终结是一连串杂乱的发生，既不是单一事件，也不是单一日期。战争的结束和条约的签署——两者都发生在基督历1491年——与穆斯林领袖的出走、基督徒旗帜的升起，或天主教君主们1492年1月6日光荣进入被征服的城市同样重要。然而，格拉纳达的投降已是正在生成的历史所能达到的最接近里程碑的东西。里程碑总是参照某个过去而设立的，而西方基督教世界为自己塑造的那个过去，把不断移动的西班牙边疆投射为十字架最南端的壁垒。

en: Since the Council of Clermont (1095), in part as an unexpected effect of three centuries of Islamic influence and control, Christian militants from both sides of the Pyrenees had heralded the reconquest of the Iberian peninsula as a sort of Christian
, the

to the Holy Land, a necessary stage on the road to the Holy Sepulchre. Popes, bishops, and kings had enlisted the limited—but highly symbolic—participation of Catholics from France to Scotland in various campaigns with such incentives as the partial remission of penance.
zh: 自克莱蒙会议（1095年）以来——部分作为三个世纪伊斯兰影响与控制的意外效果——来自比利牛斯山两侧的基督教好战者把收复伊比利亚半岛宣扬为某种基督教的
，通往圣地的
，走向圣墓的必经一站。教皇、主教和国王们以部分免除补赎之类的激励，动员了从法国到苏格兰的天主教徒投入各场战役，参与规模虽有限，象征意义却很大。

en: To be sure, cultural interpenetration between Christians, Moslems, and Jews went on in the peninsula and even north of the Pyrenees long after Alfonso Henriques took Lisbon from the Arabs and placed Portugal under the tutelage of the church early in the twelfth century.

But the rhetoric of the popes and the merger of church and state power in the Iberian dominions, which went back to the Visigoths, created an ideological space where religions and cultures that mingled in daily life were seen as officially incompatible. Within that space, the defense of a Christendom, projected as pure and besieged, became a dominant idiom for the military campaigns.
zh: 诚然，在阿方索·恩里克斯（Alfonso Henriques）于十二世纪初从阿拉伯人手中夺取里斯本、把葡萄牙置于教会庇护之下之后很久，基督徒、穆斯林和犹太人之间的文化互渗仍在半岛、乃至比利牛斯山以北继续。
但教皇们的修辞，以及伊比利亚各领地中可追溯到西哥特人的政教权力合一，造就了一个意识形态空间：在日常生活中交融的宗教与文化，在这个空间里被视为官方上互不相容。在这个空间内，保卫一个被投射为纯洁而被围困的基督教世界，成了各场军事战役的主导话语。

en: Both religious and military ardor declined in the second half of the fourteenth century, yet religion remained by default the closest thing to a “public arena” until the end of the Middle Ages, and religious figures the most able crowd leaders. Thus when religious and military enthusiasm, still intertwined, climbed together once more during Isabella’s reign, the ultimate significance of the war for Christendom resurfaced unquestioned.

Even then, though, if many of those who lived the fall of Granada saw in it an occurrence of exceptional relevance, it was a milestone only for the peculiar individuals who paid attention to such things in the first place.
zh: 宗教与军事热情在十四世纪下半叶双双衰退，然而直到中世纪结束，在缺少其他公共场合的情况下，宗教仍最接近所谓“公共舞台”，宗教人物仍是最有能力的群众领袖。因此，当仍然交织在一起的宗教与军事热情在伊莎贝拉（Isabella）治下再度一同高涨时，这场战争对基督教世界的终极意义便毫无争议地重新浮现。
即便如此，虽然许多亲历格拉纳达陷落的人视之为意义非凡的事件，它也只是对那些本来就关注此类事情的特定个人而言才是一个里程碑。

en: It mattered little then, in comparison, that a few months after entering Granada, the Catholic monarchs gave their blessing to a Genoese adventurer eager to reach India via a short-cut through the western seas.

It would matter little that the Genoese was wrong, having grossly underestimated the distance to be traveled. It probably mattered less, at the time, that the Genoese and his Castilian companions reached not the Indies but a tiny islet in the Bahamas on October 12, 1492. The landing in the Bahamas was certainly not the event of the year 1492, if only because the few who cared, on the other side of the Atlantic, did not learn about it until 1493.
zh: 相比之下，当时几乎无人在意：进入格拉纳达几个月后，天主教君主们祝福了一个热那亚冒险家，此人急于取道西海的捷径抵达印度。
这个热那亚人错了，大大低估了要走的路程——这也几乎无人在意。而在当时，这个热那亚人和他的卡斯蒂利亚同伴在1492年10月12日抵达的不是印度群岛而是巴哈马的一个小岛，恐怕更无人在意。巴哈马登陆肯定不是1492年的年度大事，单是因为大西洋彼岸少数关心此事的人直到1493年才得知消息。

en: How interesting, then, that 1492 has become Columbus’s year, and October 12 the day of “The Discovery.” Columbus himself has become a quintessential “Spaniard” or a representative of “Italy”—two rather vague entities during his lifetime. The landing has become a clear-cut event much more fixed in time than the prolonged fall of Muslim Granada, the seemingly interminable expulsion of European Jews, or the tortuous consolidation of royal power in the early Renaissance. Whereas these latter issues still appear as convoluted processes—thus the favored turf of academic specialists who break them down into an infinite list of themes for doctoral dissertations—The Discovery has lost its processual character. It has become a single and simple moment.
zh: 那么，1492年成了哥伦布之年、10月12日成了“发现”（The Discovery）之日，这是多么有趣。哥伦布本人成了一个典型的“西班牙人”或“意大利”的代表——在他有生之年，这是两个相当模糊的实体。登陆成了一个轮廓分明的事件，在时间上比穆斯林格拉纳达漫长的陷落、看似无休无止的欧洲犹太人驱逐，或文艺复兴早期王权曲折的巩固要固定得多。后面这些问题至今仍呈现为纠缠的过程——因而成为学院专家青睐的地盘，他们把这些问题拆解成无穷无尽的博士论文选题清单——而“发现”却失去了它的过程性。它成了一个单一而简单的时刻。

en: The creation of that historical moment facilitates the narrativization of history, the transformation of what happened into that which is said to have happened. First, chronology replaces process. All events are placed in a single line leading to the landfall. The years Columbus spent in Portugal, the knowledge he accumulated from Portuguese and North African sailors, his efforts to peddle his project to various monarchs are subsumed among the “antecedents” to The Discovery.

Other occurrences, such as the participation of the Pinzon brothers, are included under “the preparations,” although in the time lived by the actors, that participation preceded, overlapped, and outlived the landfall. Second, as intermingled processes fade into a linear continuity, context also fades out. For instance, the making of Europe, the rise of the absolutist state, the

, and Christian religious intransigence all spread over centuries and paralleled the invention of the Americas. These Old World transformations were not without consequences. Most notably, they created in Castile and elsewhere a number of rejects. Indeed, the first Europeans who made it to the New World were in great majority the rejects of Europe, individuals of modest means who had nothing to lose in a desperate adventure.

But in the narrative of The Discovery, Europe becomes a neutral and ageless essence able to function, in turn, as stage for “the preparations,” as background for “the voyage,” and as supportive cast in a noble epic.
zh: 那个历史时刻的创造便利了历史的叙述化，即把所发生之事转化为被说成发生之事。首先，年代顺序取代了过程。所有事件都被排进一条通向登陆的单线。哥伦布在葡萄牙度过的岁月、他从葡萄牙和北非水手那里积累的知识、他向各国君主兜售其计划的努力，都被归入“发现”的“前因”。
其他发生之事，比如平松兄弟（Pinzon brothers）的参与，则被归入“筹备”，尽管在行动者所经历的时间里，这种参与先于登陆、与登陆交叠、并在登陆之后延续。其次，随着相互交织的过程淡化为线性连续，语境也淡出了。例如，欧洲的造就、绝对主义国家的兴起、
和基督教的不妥协，都绵延数个世纪，与美洲的发明并行。这些旧世界的转变并非没有后果。最显著的是，它们在卡斯蒂利亚和别处制造了一批弃儿。的确，第一批抵达新世界的欧洲人绝大多数是欧洲的弃儿，是些家境平平、即使孤注一掷失败也没有什么可再失去的人。
但在“发现”的叙述中，欧洲变成了一种中立、仿佛超越时代的本质，可以依次充当“筹备”的舞台、“航行”的背景，以及一部高贵史诗中的配角阵容。

en: The isolation of a single moment thus creates a historical “fact”: on this day, in 1492, Christopher Columbus discovered the Bahamas. As a set event, void of context and marked by a fixed date, this chunk of history becomes much more manageable outside of the academic guild. It returns inevitably: one can await its millenial and prepare its commemoration. It accommodates travel agents, airlines, politicians, the media, or the states who sell it in the prepackaged forms by which the public has come to expect history to present itself for immediate consumption. It is a product of power whose label has been cleansed of traces of power.
zh: 于是，对单一时刻的孤立创造出一个历史“事实”：1492年的这一天，克里斯托弗·哥伦布发现了巴哈马。作为一个被框定的事件，抽空了语境、标定了固定日期，这一块历史在学院行会之外变得好处理得多。它必然回返：人们可以等待它的千年纪念（原文 millenial，当作 millennial），筹备它的庆典。它迎合旅行社、航空公司、政客、媒体，或那些把它打包出售的国家——公众已经期待历史以这种预包装的形式呈现，供即时消费。这是一件权力的产品，其标签上的权力痕迹已被清洗干净。

en: The naming of the “fact” is itself a narrative of power disguised as innocence. Would anyone care to celebrate the “Castilian invasion of the Bahamas”? Yet this phrasing is somewhat closer to what happened on October 12, 1492, than “the discovery of America.” Naming the fact thus already imposes a reading and many historical controversies boil down to who has the power to name what. To call “discovery” the first invasions of inhabited lands by Europeans is an exercise in Eurocentric power that already frames future narratives of the event so described. Contact with the West is seen as the foundation of historicity of different cultures.
Once discovered by Europeans, the Other finally enters the human world.
zh: 给这个“事实”命名，本身就是一个伪装成天真的权力叙述。有谁愿意庆祝“卡斯蒂利亚人对巴哈马的入侵”？然而比起“美洲的发现”，这个措辞还更接近1492年10月12日实际发生的事。给事实命名因此已经强加了一种读解，许多历史争论归根结底是谁有权命名什么。把欧洲人对有人居住的土地的最初入侵称为“发现”，是一种欧洲中心主义权力的行使，它已经框定了未来对所描述事件的叙述。与西方的接触被视为不同文化之历史性的奠基。
一旦被欧洲人发现，他者才终于进入人类世界。

en: In the 1990s, quite a few observers, historians, and activists worldwide denounced the arrogance implied by this terminology during the quincentennial celebrations of Columbus’s Bahamian landing. Some spoke of a Columbian Holocaust. Some proposed “conquest” instead of discovery; others preferred “encounter,” which suddenly gained an immense popularity—one more testimony, if needed, of the capacity of liberal discourse to compromise between its premises and its practice.
“Encounter” sweetens the horror, polishes the rough edges that do not fit neatly either side of the controversy. Everyone seems to gain.
zh: 在1990年代哥伦布巴哈马登陆五百周年的庆典期间，世界各地相当多的观察者、历史学家和活动人士谴责了这一术语隐含的傲慢。有人称之为哥伦布大屠杀（Columbian Holocaust）。有人提议用“征服”取代发现；另一些人偏爱“相遇”（encounter），这个词突然大受欢迎——如果还需要证据的话，这再次证明了自由主义话语在其前提与实践之间妥协的能力。
“相遇”给恐怖裹上糖衣，磨平了那些无法整齐归入争论任何一方的粗糙棱角。似乎人人都是赢家。

en: Not everyone was convinced. Portuguese historian Vitorino Magalhaes Godinho, a former minister of education, reiterated that “discovery” was an appropriate term for the European ventures of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, which he compares to Herschel’s discovery of Uranus, and Sédillot’s discovery of microbes.
The problem is, of course, that Uranus did not know that it existed before Herschel, and that Sédillot did not go after the microbes with a sword and a gun.
zh: 并非人人都被说服。葡萄牙历史学家维托里诺·马加良斯·戈迪尼奥（Vitorino Magalhaes Godinho）——一位前教育部长——重申“发现”是描述十五、十六世纪欧洲冒险事业的恰当用词，他把这些事业比作赫歇尔（Herschel）发现天王星，以及塞迪约（Sédillot）发现微生物。
问题当然在于：天王星在赫歇尔之前并不知道自己存在，而塞迪约也没有带着刀剑和枪炮去追猎微生物。

en: Yet more than blind arrogance is at issue here. Terminologies demarcate a field, politically and epistemologically. Names set up a field of power.

“Discovery” and analogous terms ensure that by just mentioning the event one enters a predetermined lexical field of clichés and predictable categories that foreclose a redefinition of the political and intellectual stakes. Europe becomes the center of “what happened.” Whatever else may have happened

other peoples in that process is already reduced to a natural fact: they were discovered. The similarity to planets and microbes precedes their explicit mention by future historians and cabinet ministers.
zh: 然而这里的问题不止是盲目的傲慢。术语在政治上和认识论上划定一个场域。名称设立一个权力场。
“发现”及类似用词确保：只要提及该事件，人就进入一个由陈词滥调和可预测范畴构成的预定词汇场，从而堵死了对政治与思想利害的重新定义。欧洲成了“所发生之事”的中心。无论其他民族在那个过程中还
了什么，都已被还原为一个自然事实：他们被发现了。行星和微生物的类比，早在后世的历史学家和内阁部长明说以前就已蕴含在这套用词里。

en: For this reason, I prefer to say that Columbus “stumbled on the Bahamas,” or “discovered the Antilles,” and I prefer “conquest” over “discovery” to describe what happened after the landing. Such phrasings are awkward and may raise some eyebrows. They may even annoy some readers. But both the awkwardness and the fact that the entire issue can be dismissed as trivial quibbling suggests that it is not easy to subvert the very language describing the facts of the matter. For the power to decide what is trivial—and annoying—is also part of the power to decide how “what happened” becomes “that which is said to have happened.”
zh: 正因如此，我宁愿说哥伦布“撞上了巴哈马”，或“发现了安的列斯群岛”，而在描述登陆之后发生的事时，我宁愿用“征服”而非“发现”。这类措辞很别扭，可能让一些人挑眉，甚至可能惹恼一些读者。但无论是这种别扭，还是整个问题可以被当作琐碎的咬文嚼字打发掉这一事实，都表明：要颠覆描述事实本身的语言并不容易。因为决定什么是琐碎——以及什么惹人烦——的权力，也是决定“所发生之事”如何变成“被说成发生之事”的权力的一部分。

en: Here again, power enters into the interface between historicity 1 and historicity 2. The triviality clause—for it is a clause, not an argument—forbids describing what happened from the point of view of some of the people who saw it happen or to whom it happened. It is a form of archival power. With the exercise of that power, “facts” become clear, sanitized.
zh: 在这里，权力再次进入历史性1与历史性2之间的界面。琐碎化条款——因为它是一个条款，不是一个论证——禁止从某些目睹事件发生或事件降临于其身的人的视角来描述所发生之事。这是档案权力的一种形式。随着这种权力的行使，“事实”显得一清二楚，不堪的部分也被抹去了。

en: Commemorations sanitize further the messy history lived by the actors. They contribute to the continuous myth-making process that gives history its more definite shapes: they help to create, modify, or sanction the public meanings attached to historical events deemed worthy of mass celebration. As rituals that package history for public consumption, commemorations play the numbers game to create a past that seems both more real and more elementary.
zh: 纪念活动进一步抹平行动者所经历的历史中混乱而难堪的部分。它们参与那个持续的神话制造过程，正是这个过程赋予历史更确定的形状：它们帮助创造、修改或批准那些附加在被认为值得大众庆祝的历史事件上的公共意义。作为把历史打包供公众消费的仪式，纪念活动玩数字游戏，以创造一个显得既更真实又更简单的过去。

en: Numbers matter at the end point, the consumption side of the game: the greater the number of participants in a celebration, the stronger the allusion to the multitude of witnesses for whom the mythicized event is supposed to have meant something from day one. In 1992, when millions of people celebrated a quincentennial staged by states, advertisers, and travel agents, their very mass reinforced the illusion that Columbus’s contemporaries must have known—how could they not?—that October 12, 1492, was indeed a momentous event. As we have seen, it was not; and many of our contemporaries, for various reasons, said as much. But few of the 1992 celebrants could accentuate publicly the banality of that date, five hundred years before, without having to admit also that power had intervened between the event and its celebration.
zh: 数字在终点、在游戏的消费端起作用：庆典的参与者越多，就越强烈地暗示有众多见证者——据说被神话化的事件从第一天起就对他们意味着什么。1992年，当数百万人庆祝一场由国家、广告商和旅行社操办的五百周年时，他们的人数本身就强化了那种幻觉：哥伦布的同时代人必定知道——他们怎么可能不知道？——1492年10月12日确实是一个重大时刻。如我们所见，事实并非如此；而我们的许多同时代人也出于各种原因这样说了。但1992年的庆祝者中，很少有人能在公开强调那个日期在五百年前的平淡无奇时，不必同时承认权力曾介入事件与其庆典之间。

en: The more varied the participants, the easier also the claim to world historical significance.

Numbers matter also as items in the calendar. Years, months, and dates present history as part of the natural cycles of the world. By packaging events within temporal sequences, commemorations adorn the past with certainty: the proof of the happening is in the cyclical inevitability of its celebration.
zh: 参与者越多样，就越容易声称这件事具有世界历史意义。
数字作为历法中的项目也很重要。年、月、日把历史呈现为世界自然循环的一部分。通过把事件包装进时间序列，纪念活动给过去饰以确定性：庆典每到一定周期就必然举行，仿佛因此便能证明事件当时确曾如此发生。

en: Cycles may vary, of course, but annual cycles provide a basic element of modern commemorations: an exact date.

As a tool of historical production, that date anchors the event in the present. It does so through the simultaneous production of mentions and silences. The recurrence of a predictable date severs Columbus’s landfall from the context of emerging Europe on and around 1492. It obliterates the rest of the year now subsumed within a twenty-four hour segment. It imposes a silence upon all events surrounding the one being marked. A potentially endless void now encompasses everything that could be said and is not being said about 1492 and about the years immediately preceding or following.
zh: 循环当然可以不同，但年度循环提供了现代纪念的一个基本要素：一个确切的日期。
作为历史生产的工具，这个日期把事件锚定在当下。它通过同时生产提及与沉默来做到这一点。一个可预测日期的反复出现，把哥伦布的登陆从1492年前后正在崛起的欧洲的语境中割裂出来。它抹去了如今被归入一个二十四小时片段的这一年其余部分。它对围绕被标记事件的所有事件强加一种沉默。一个可能无尽的虚空，如今囊括了关于1492年及其前后紧邻年份本可以说而未被说出的一切。

en: The void, however, is not left unfilled. The fixed date alone places the event within a new frame with linkages of its own. As a fixed date, October 12 is the fetishized repository for a potentially endless list of disparate events, such as the birth of U.S. activist Dick Gregory or that of Italian tenor Luciano Pavarotti; the independence of Equatorial Guinea; the Broadway opening of the musical

; or the refusal of a Catholic monk, one Martin Luther, to repudiate assertions posted months before on the door of a church in Germany. All these events happened on October 12 of the Christian calendar, in various years from 1518 to 1971. All are likely to be acknowledged publicly by varying numbers of milestone worshippers. Each of them, in turn, can be replaced by another event judged to be equally—or more—noteworthy: Paraguay’s break from Argentina in 1811, the 1976 arrest of the Chinese Gang of Four, the beginning of the German occupation of France in 1914, or the approval of the Magna Carta by Edward I of England in 1297.
zh: 然而，虚空不会被留空。固定日期本身就把事件置入一个自有其关联的新框架。作为一个固定日期，10月12日成了一个被拜物化的仓库，容纳一份可能无尽的杂异事件清单：美国活动人士迪克·格雷戈里（Dick Gregory）或意大利男高音卢恰诺·帕瓦罗蒂（Luciano Pavarotti）的出生；赤道几内亚的独立；音乐剧

在百老汇的首演；或一位名叫马丁·路德的天主教修士拒绝撤回几个月前张贴在德国一座教堂门上的主张。所有这些事件都发生在基督历10月12日，年份从1518年到1971年不等。它们都可能被数目不等的里程碑崇拜者公开承认。而它们中的每一个，又都可以被另一个被认为同样——或更加——值得注意的事件取代：1811年巴拉圭脱离阿根廷，1976年中国“四人帮”被捕，1914年德国对法国占领的开始，或1297年英格兰国王爱德华一世对《大宪章》的重申。
body.review: 底本将1976年“四人帮”被捕列入例举，隔离审查实际发生于10月6日。里尔市档案馆记载德军于1914年10月12日进入里尔，底本这里概称德国对法国占领的开始。美国国家档案馆所藏1297年《大宪章》重申本署10月12日。

en: The roster is theoretically expandable in any direction. If the Magna Carta is the most ancient icon mentioned here, that is because these examples have come from the institutionalized memory of what is now the West and were all indexed through Dionysius Exiguus’s system. With other modes of counting and another pool of events, October 12 of the Christian calendar could overlap in any given year a number of anniversaries next to which the landing in the Bahamas would look quite recent. As arbitrary markers of time, dates link a number of dissimilar events, all equally decontextualized and equally susceptible to mythicization. The longer the list of events celebrated on the same date, the more that list looks like an answer in a trivia game. But this is precisely because celebrations trivialize the historical process (historicity 1) at the same time that they mythicize history (historicity 2).
zh: 这份名单理论上可以向任何方向扩展。如果说《大宪章》是这里提到的最早的历史象征，那是因为这些例子都来自如今所谓西方的制度化记忆，全都通过小狄奥尼修斯的纪年体系编入索引。换用其他计数方式和另一个事件库，基督历的10月12日在任何给定年份都可能与一批周年纪念日重叠，相比之下巴哈马登陆会显得相当晚近。作为时间的任意标记，日期把一批互不相似的事件连接起来，它们同样被去语境化，同样易于被神话化。在同一日期庆祝的事件清单越长，这份清单就越像冷知识竞猜里的一个答案。但这恰恰是因为庆典在把历史（历史性2）神话化的同时，把历史过程（历史性1）琐碎化了。

en: The myth-making process does not operate evenly, however, and the preceding list suggests as much. For if—in theory—all events can be decontextualized to the same point of emptiness, in practice not all are reshaped by the same power plays and not all mean the same to new actors entering the stage and busily reformulating and appropriating the past. In short, celebrations are created, and this creation is part and parcel of the process of historical production. Celebrations straddle the two sides of historicity. They impose a silence upon the events that they ignore, and they fill that silence with narratives of power about the event they celebrate.
zh: 然而，神话制造过程并不均匀地运作，前面那份清单已暗示了这一点。因为如果说——在理论上——所有事件都能被去语境化到同一个空洞的点上，那么在实践中，并非所有事件都被同样的权力游戏重塑，也并非所有事件对登台忙于重新表述和占用过去的新行动者意味着同样的东西。简言之，庆典是被创造出来的，而这种创造是历史生产过程不可分割的一部分。庆典横跨历史性的两侧。它们对被其忽略的事件强加沉默，又用关于所庆祝事件的权力叙述填满那个沉默。

en: The reasons to celebrate Columbus Day and to do so on October 12 are now obvious to most Americans, just as the rationale behind the quincentennial was obvious to many in the West. Most advocates of these celebrations will evoke the obvious significance of “what happened” in 1492 and the no less obvious consequences of that event. But the road between then and now is no more straightforward than the relation between what happened and what is said to have happened. October 12 was certainly not a historical landmark in Columbus’s day. It took centuries of battles—both petty and grandiose—and quite a bit of luck to turn it into a significant date. Further, not all those who agree now that the date and the event it indexes are important agree on the significance of its celebration. The images and debates that surround the appropriation of Columbus vary from Spain to the United States and from both Spain and the United States to Latin America, to mention only three areas treated in this chapter.

Constructions of Columbus and of Columbus Day vary within these areas according to time and also according to factors such as class and ethnic identification. In short, the road between then and now is itself a history of power.
zh: 如今，对大多数美国人来说，庆祝哥伦布日、并在10月12日庆祝的理由是显而易见的，正如五百周年的道理对许多西方人显而易见一样。这些庆典的大多数拥护者会搬出1492年“所发生之事”的显而易见的意义，以及该事件同样显而易见的后果。但从那时到现在的道路，并不比所发生之事与被说成发生之事之间的关系更直截了当。10月12日在哥伦布的时代肯定不是一个历史地标。它花了几个世纪的争斗——既有小打小闹也有宏大排场——外加不少运气，才变成一个有意义的日期。再者，并非所有如今同意这个日期及其所指事件很重要的人，都同意庆祝它的意义。各方把哥伦布纳入自己的历史叙述时所塑造的形象、引发的争论，从西班牙到美国各不相同，从西、美两国到拉丁美洲又各不相同——这里只提本章处理的三个地区。
在这些地区内部，哥伦布与哥伦布日的建构随时间而变，也随阶级和族群认同之类的因素而变。简言之，从那时到现在的道路本身就是一部权力的历史。

en: An Anniversary in the Making
zh: 一个正在生成的周年纪念日

en: Columbus was not treated as a favorite hero by nascent Spain, nor was October 12 marked as a special day during his lifetime. To be sure, the landing in the Bahamas, the verified existence of an American landmass, the integration of the Caribbean in the European orbit, and the imperial reorganizations that paralleled these events imposed a symbolic reordering of the world which, in turn, contributed to the wealth of myths that now define the West—Utopia, the noble savage, the white man’s burden, among others.

Still, it took quite a few years of intense struggles over political and economic power in Europe and the Americas for the narrative to unfold in ways that acknowledged the discovery as event and the discoverer as hero. Indeed it took a living hero, Charles V, and his pretensions to a Catholic empire stretching from Tunis to Lima and from Vienna to Vera Cruz for Columbus, then dead, to become a hero. In 1552, Francisco López de Gómara suggested to Charles that the most important event in history—after the divine Creation of the world and the Coming of Christ—was the conquest of the Americas.
zh: 新生的西班牙并没有把哥伦布当作宠爱的英雄，10月12日在他有生之年也没有被标为特殊的日子。诚然，巴哈马登陆、美洲陆块存在的证实、加勒比被纳入欧洲轨道，以及与这些事件并行的帝国重组，强加了一种对世界的象征性重排，而这种重排又助长了如今定义西方的那套神话——乌托邦、高贵的野蛮人、白人的负担（the white man’s burden），等等。

尽管如此，欧洲和美洲围绕政治与经济权力的激烈争斗又持续了好些年，叙述才展开到承认发现是事件、发现者是英雄的地步。事实上，要等到一位活着的英雄——查理五世（Charles V）——和他对一个从突尼斯延伸到利马、从维也纳延伸到韦拉克鲁斯的天主教帝国的野心，已死的哥伦布才成了英雄。1552年，弗朗西斯科·洛佩斯·德·戈马拉（Francisco López de Gómara）向查理提出：历史上最重要的事件——仅次于上帝创世和基督降临——是美洲的征服。

en: Even then, there was no “public” celebration. When López de Gómara wrote these lines, the Castilians who lived on American soil had already measured the gaps between the dream of a New World and the realities of their daily life under an increasingly heavy colonial bureaucracy. Columbus’s first group of admirers was restricted, at best, to a few Spanish intellectuals and bureaucrats. Further, even as Spanish arts and themes gained international attention during the reign of Philip II, the sinking of the armada in 1588 had already suggested other times and priorities. By the early seventeenth century, the conquest of the Americas was as much a miscellany of efforts by French, Dutch, and British adventurers as a competition between the Iberian states. The northern Europeans who benefited most from the rise of Caribbean plantations and trans-Atlantic trade during the two centuries following Philip’s reign tended to commission paintings of themselves and their families rather than writings about conquistadores. Meanwhile, among the intellectual elites of Europe, the mythicized faces of America overshadowed that of Columbus.
zh: 即便如此，当时也没有“公共”庆典。洛佩斯·德·戈马拉写下这些句子时，生活在美洲土地上的卡斯蒂利亚人已经丈量过新世界之梦与他们在日益沉重的殖民官僚体制下的日常生活现实之间的差距。哥伦布最早的崇拜者群体，往好里说也仅限于少数西班牙知识分子和官僚。再者，尽管西班牙艺术与题材在腓力二世（Philip II）治下赢得国际关注，1588年无敌舰队的沉没已经暗示了别样的时势与优先事项。到十七世纪初，美洲的征服既是法国、荷兰和英国冒险家各显身手的杂集，也是伊比利亚国家之间的竞争。在腓力治世之后两个世纪里，从加勒比种植园和跨大西洋贸易的兴起中获益最多的北欧人，倾向于委托画师为自己和家人画像，而不是委托文人撰写征服者（conquistadores）的故事。与此同时，在欧洲知识精英中间，美洲被神话化的面孔盖过了哥伦布的面孔。

en: Thus it was in the New World itself that Columbus could first emerge most strongly as myth, in the former colonies of Spain and in the United States. The United States was one of the few places where the growth of a modern public in the midst of the Enlightenment was not encumbered by images of a feudal past. There, as elsewhere, the constitution of a public domain reflected the organization of power and the development of the national state, but power was constituted differently from the way it took shape in most European countries. Citizens with a weakness for marching bands promoted celebrations and holidays more openly and often more successfully than in Europe.
zh: 因此，哥伦布最早能最强烈地作为神话浮现的地方，是新世界本身——西班牙的前殖民地和美利坚合众国。美国是少数几个在启蒙之中培育现代公众、却不受封建过去形象拖累的地方之一。在那里，和别处一样，公共领域的构成反映了权力的组织与民族国家的发展，但权力的构成方式不同于它在大多数欧洲国家成形的方式。偏爱行进乐队的公民们推动庆典和节日，比在欧洲更公开，也往往更成功。

en: The Tammany Society, or Columbian Order, an otherwise clannish group of gentlemen incorporated in New York in 1789, had such a taste for public attention, parades and lavish banquets. Their list of celebrations included Washington’s birthday and the Fourth of July, but also Bastille Day and other international milestones they deemed worthy of recognition. Columbus’s landfall figured on their first calendar, published in 1790. More important, by what seems to be a historical accident (the joint effect of fixed dates, fund-raising opportunities, and political fortunes), their most lavish ceremony occurred on October 12, 1792. On that day, members organized a memorable banquet and erected a fourteen-foot-high monument to Columbus that they promised to illuminate annually on the anniversary of the landfall. They did not keep that promise. Still, their banquet was remembered almost a hundred years later, when new groups of worshipers searched for a North American precedent for Columbus Day.
zh: 坦慕尼协会（Tammany Society），又称哥伦布团（Columbian Order），是1789年在纽约注册的绅士团体。这些平日相当排外的人却热衷于引人瞩目，也喜欢游行和奢华宴会。他们的庆典清单包括华盛顿诞辰和七月四日独立日，但也包括巴士底日和其他他们认为值得承认的国际里程碑。哥伦布登陆列在他们1790年出版的第一份日历上。更重要的是，出于似乎是历史偶然的原因（固定日期、筹款机会和政治运气的共同作用），他们最奢华的典礼发生在1792年10月12日。那一天，成员们组织了一场令人难忘的宴会，并竖立了一座十四英尺高的哥伦布纪念碑，承诺每年在登陆周年纪念日点亮它。他们没有兑现那个承诺。尽管如此，他们的宴会在将近一百年后仍被人记起——当时新一批崇拜者正在为哥伦布日寻找一个北美的先例。

en: Latin America, meanwhile, kept Columbus’s image alive but treated it with ambivalence until the late 1880s. Some territories fought Europe repeatedly over Columbus’s remains, both literally and figuratively. Two Caribbean colonies competed with Spain for Columbus’s long-dead body.

The independent state that emerged from Bolívar’s armed struggle on the mainland claimed Columbus’s name both before and after the secession of Venezuela and Ecuador from Gran Colombia. Still, even though the Latin American rejection of Spanish political tutelage did not entail a rejection of
, early ideologies of independence and, later, Spain’s Ten Years War against Cuba (1868–1878) hampered the complete integration of Columbus into the pantheon of South American heroes.
zh: 与此同时，拉丁美洲让哥伦布的形象保持鲜活，却以矛盾的态度对待它，直到1880年代末。一些领地一再与欧洲争夺哥伦布的遗骸——既是字面意义也是比喻意义上的。两个加勒比殖民地与西班牙争夺哥伦布早已死去的身体。
从玻利瓦尔（Bolívar）在大陆的武装斗争中诞生的独立国家，在委内瑞拉和厄瓜多尔脱离大哥伦比亚（Gran Colombia）之前和之后，都以哥伦布的名字命名自己。尽管如此，虽然拉丁美洲对西班牙的政治管辖的拒绝并不必然意味着拒绝
，早期的独立意识形态，以及后来西班牙对古巴的十年战争（1868–1878），都妨碍了哥伦布完全进入南美英雄的万神殿。

en: Ethnicity—or rather, ideologies of ethnicity—added to Latin America’s ambivalence toward Columbus. Latin American ideologies attribute to the New World situation an active role in the making of socio-racial categories. It is not simply that categories require new names (
) or new ingredients under old names (
); the rules by which they are devised are different from those of Europe and acknowledged as such.

Discourses intertwined with these rules and reproducing the Creole categories give a central role, implicit or explicit, to metaphors of “blending” in spite of the age-old denigration of certain cultural traditions and in spite of systems of stratification that manipulate the perception of phenotypes. Skewed as it was, a blending did occur.
zh: 族群性——或者更确切地说，关于族群性的意识形态——加重了拉丁美洲对哥伦布的矛盾态度。拉丁美洲的意识形态赋予新世界的处境一个主动角色：社会与种族分类的形成。问题不只是这些范畴需要新名称（
），或旧名称下的新成分（
）；它们被制定出来的规则不同于欧洲的规则，而且被承认就是不同。
与这些规则交织、再生产克里奥尔范畴的话语，赋予“融合”隐喻一个或隐或显的中心角色，尽管某些文化传统遭受着由来已久的贬损，尽管分层系统在操纵着人们对表型的感知。尽管有所偏斜，融合确实发生了。

en: Brutal as it was also, Spanish colonization did not nearly wipe out pre-Conquest Americans in the southern landmass as the Anglos did in the north or as Spaniards themselves did in the Caribbean islands, if only because the aboriginal populations of both Mexico and the Andes were enormous. Early cultural practices often intertwined European and native elements. Early manifestations of a distinct local identity included some sense of “Indianness.” Historian Stuart Schwartz draws on Fernando de Azedevo to observe that in certain regions of Brazil, “Tupí, the predominant Indian language, was more widely spoken than Portuguese … even by the colonists.”

Later, political doctrines of the nineteenth century incorporated both the metaphors of a blend and the acknowledgment of the Indian, even while the organization of power kept Indians and Afro-Latins outside the decision-making process. Hence, Bolívar could declare in 1815: “We are … neither Indian nor European, but a species midway between the legitimate proprietors of this country and the Spanish usurpers.”

A few decades later, nineteenth-century scientific racism did influence Latin American opinions and practices, albeit without always negating the stress on mixes rather than pure sets, on differences of degree rather than differences of kind.
zh: 西班牙的殖民同样残酷，但它并没有像盎格鲁人在北方、或西班牙人自己在加勒比群岛那样，几乎灭绝南部大陆上前征服时代的美洲原住民，单是因为墨西哥和安第斯的原住民人口都极为庞大。早期的文化实践常常把欧洲与原住民元素交织在一起。一种独特的地方认同的早期表现，包含某种“印第安性”的意识。历史学家斯图尔特·施瓦茨（Stuart Schwartz）援引费尔南多·德·阿泽德沃（Fernando de Azedevo）指出，在巴西某些地区，“占主导地位的印第安语言图皮语（Tupí）比葡萄牙语使用得更广……甚至连殖民者也在说”。
后来，十九世纪的政治学说既纳入了融合的隐喻，也纳入了对印第安人的承认，尽管权力的组织仍把印第安人和非洲裔拉美人排除在决策过程之外。因此，玻利瓦尔能在1815年宣称：“我们……既不是印第安人也不是欧洲人，而是介于这片土地的合法所有者与西班牙篡夺者之间的一类人。”
几十年后，十九世纪的科学种族主义确实影响了拉丁美洲的观点与实践，尽管并不总是否定那种强调混合而非纯粹集合、强调程度差异而非种类差异的取向。

en: In short, for many reasons too complex to detail here, Latin Americans did not alienate native cultures from their myths of origin, even before the twentieth-century rise of various forms of
They view themselves as
and
of different kinds, peoples of the New World; perhaps Columbus was too much a man of the Old.
zh: 简言之，出于许多复杂得无法在此详述的原因，拉丁美洲人没有把原住民文化从他们的起源神话中剥离出去，甚至早在二十世纪各种形式的
兴起之前就是如此。他们把自己看作不同种类的
和
，新世界的人民；也许哥伦布太是一个旧世界的人了。

en: In the United States, in contrast, in spite of inflated references to a melting pot, ideologies of ethnicity emphasize continuities with the

World. The real natives are mainly dead or on reservations. New natives (recognizable by their hyphenated group names) are numbered by generation, and their descendants fight each other for pieces of a mythical Europe. The peculiar politics of ethnicity has proved to be a boon for Columbus’s image in the United States.
zh: 相比之下，在美国，尽管有对熔炉（melting pot）的夸大指称，族群性意识形态强调的却是与
世界的连续性。真正的原住民大多死了，或在保留地上。新的“本地人”（凭他们带连字符的群体名称即可辨认）按代际计数，他们的后代为一块块神话化的欧洲彼此争斗。这种独特的族群政治被证明给哥伦布的形象在美国走红创造了有利条件。

en: Ethnicity gave Columbus a lobby, a prerequisite to public success in U.S. culture. The 1850 census reported only 3,679 individuals of Italian birth. Yet by 1866, Italian-Americans, organized by the Sharpshooters’ Association of New York, celebrated the landfall and, within three years, annual festivities were being held in Philadelphia, St. Louis, Boston, Cincinnati, New Orleans, and San Francisco on or around October 12.

Italians and Spaniards were just not enough, however, to turn this celebration into a national practice. Fortunately, ethnicity gave Columbus a second—and more numerous—group of lobbyists, Irish-Americans.
zh: 族群性给了哥伦布一个游说集团——这是在美国文化中取得公共成功的先决条件。1850年人口普查报告的意大利出生者只有3679人。然而到1866年，由纽约神枪手协会（Sharpshooters’ Association of New York）组织起来的意大利裔美国人已经在庆祝登陆，三年之内，费城、圣路易斯、波士顿、辛辛那提、新奥尔良和旧金山都在10月12日当天或前后举行年度庆典。
然而，仅靠意大利人和西班牙人，还不足以把这个庆典变成全国性的惯例。幸运的是，族群性给了哥伦布第二批——也是人数更多的——游说者：爱尔兰裔美国人。

en: By 1850, there were already 962,000 Americans claiming Irish descent. Many of them regrouped in organizations like the Knights of Columbus, a fraternal society for Catholic males founded in 1881. In less than ten years, community support and the institutional patronage of the Catholic church swelled the Knights’ membership. As the association spread in the northeast with the backing of prominent Irish-Americans, it increasingly emphasized the shaping of “citizen culture.”

Columbus played a leading role in making citizens out of these immigrants. He provided them with a public example of Catholic devotion and civic virtue, and thus a powerful rejoinder to the cliché that allegiance to Rome preempted the Catholics’ attachment to the United States. In New Haven, the 1892 celebration of the landing attracted some forty thousand people—including six thousand Knights and a thousand-piece band conducted by the musical director of West Point—in a joint celebration of holiness and patriotism.
zh: 到1850年，已有96.2万美国人自称爱尔兰后裔。他们中许多人集结在哥伦布骑士团（Knights of Columbus）之类的组织里，这是一个1881年成立的天主教男性兄弟会。不到十年，社区支持和天主教会的机构庇护使骑士团人数激增。随着该协会在知名爱尔兰裔美国人的支持下向东北部扩展，它日益强调“公民文化”的塑造。
哥伦布在把这些移民变成公民的过程中扮演了主角。他为他们提供了一个天主教虔诚与公民美德的公共榜样，从而有力回击了那种陈词滥调：对罗马的效忠会取代天主教徒对美国的依恋。在纽黑文，1892年的登陆庆典吸引了约四万人——包括六千名骑士团员和一支由西点军校音乐总监指挥的千人乐队——共同庆祝神圣与爱国。

en: The success of these festivities was not due solely to Catholic-Americans’ desire for acceptance, nor was the cult of Columbus limited to Catholics. The introduction of history into the school curriculum as a required subject in the early nineteenth century and its slow growth before the Civil War also contributed to familiarizing a larger audience with Columbus.

So did the few biographical sketches published in the first half of the century. Nevertheless, the Catholic connection was crucial in that Catholics provided the bodies that made possible the mass celebrations of Columbus Day before the 1890s. By the 1890s, Italian and Irish efforts to promote Columbus Day in the United States coincided with—and ultimately were subsumed within—the production of two mass media events, the international celebrations of the quadricentennial of the Bahamas landfall respectively sponsored by Spain and the United States.
zh: 这些庆典的成功，不仅仅归因于美国天主教徒渴望被接纳，对哥伦布的崇拜也不限于天主教徒。十九世纪初历史作为必修课进入学校课程，以及它在内战前的缓慢发展，也帮助更大的受众熟悉了哥伦布。
世纪上半叶出版的少数几篇传记速写同样如此。尽管如此，天主教关联仍是关键，因为在1890年代之前，正是成群参加活动的天主教徒，使哥伦布日得以办成大众庆典。到1890年代，意大利裔和爱尔兰裔在美国推动哥伦布日的努力，恰与两场大众媒体事件的生产相重合——并最终被纳入其中——那就是分别由西班牙和美国赞助的巴哈马登陆四百周年的国际庆典。

en: The Castilian and the Yankee
zh: 卡斯蒂利亚人与扬基佬

en: The second half of the nineteenth century saw an unprecedented attention to the systematic management of public discourse in countries that combined substantial working classes and wide electoral franchises. With the realization that “the public”—this rather vague presumption of the first bourgeois revolutions—indeed existed, government officials, entrepreneurs, and intellectuals joined in the planned production of traditions that cut across class identities and reinforced the national state. Nationalist parades multiplied in Europe, while government imposed a daily homage to the flag in public schools in the United States. International fairs that attracted millions of visitors to London, Paris, and Philadelphia; academic conferences (such as the first congress of Orientalists in 1873), and official commemorations (such as the 1880 invention of Bastille Day, in France) taught the new masses who they were, in part by telling them who they were not. Socialists, anarchists, and working-class political activists replied in kind by publicizing their own heroes and promoting celebrations such as May Day. Public history was in the air.
zh: 十九世纪下半叶，在那些既有庞大工人阶级又有广泛选举权的国家，出现了对公共话语的系统化管理前所未有的关注。随着人们意识到“公众”——早期资产阶级革命中这个相当模糊的假定——确实存在，政府官员、企业家和知识分子联手有计划地生产跨越阶级认同、强化民族国家的传统。民族主义游行在欧洲成倍增加，而美国政府则在公立学校强制推行每日向国旗致敬。吸引数百万访客前往伦敦、巴黎和费城的国际博览会；学术会议（如1873年第一届东方学家大会）；以及官方纪念活动（如1880年法国对巴士底日的发明），都在教导新的大众他们是谁——部分是通过告诉他们他们不是谁。社会主义者、无政府主义者和工人阶级政治活动家以同样的方式回应，宣传他们自己的英雄，推动五一节之类的庆典。公共历史蔚然成风。

en: This fast-moving fin-de-siècle era caught Spain in a state of decline. Torn by factional feuds, outflanked in Europe by nearly all the Atlantic states, threatened in the Americas by the economic incursions of Britain, the influence of the United States, and the constant fear of losing Cuba, Spain was in dire need of a moral and political uplift.

Conservative leader Antonio Cánovas del Castillo, architect of the Bourbon Restoration and a historian in his own right, made of Columbus and The Discovery the consummate metaphors for this anticipated revitalization.
zh: 这个飞速变动的世纪末（fin-de-siècle）时代，撞上的是处于衰落中的西班牙。派系争斗撕裂着它，在欧洲它几乎被所有大西洋国家甩在身后，在美洲它受到英国经济渗透、美国影响以及失去古巴的持续恐惧的威胁——西班牙急需一场道德与政治的提振。
保守党领袖安东尼奥·卡诺瓦斯·德尔·卡斯蒂略（Antonio Cánovas del Castillo），波旁复辟的设计师、本身也是历史学家，把哥伦布和“发现”变成了这场预期复兴的完美隐喻。

en: Interest in Columbus had grown in the 1800s. The number of biographical sketches published in Europe and the Americas increased significantly after the 1830s. So did various suggestions of a quadricentennial in the 1880s. Cánovas turned this growing interest into an extravaganza: a political and diplomatic crusade, an economic venture, a spectacle to be consumed by Spain and the world for the sheer sake of its pageantry. The commemoration became a powerful tool with which the politician-historian and his quadricentennial junta of academics and bureaucrats wrote a narrative of The Discovery with Spain as the main character. In the words of its most thorough chronicler, the Spanish quadricentennial was “the apex of the Restoration.”
zh: 对哥伦布的兴趣在十九世纪不断增长。1830年代之后，欧洲和美洲出版的传记速写数量显著增加。1880年代关于举办四百周年的各种提议也是如此。卡诺瓦斯把这种增长的兴趣变成了一场盛大演出：一场声势浩大的政治与外交运动，一桩经济事业，一场纯粹为其排场而供西班牙和世界消费的景观。纪念活动成了一件有力的工具，这位政治家-历史学家和他由学者与官僚组成的四百周年委员会用它写出了一部以西班牙为主角的“发现”叙述。用其最详尽的编年记录者的话说，西班牙的四百周年是“复辟的顶点”。

en: Spain spent more than two and a half million pesetas and four years of preparation on the celebration. Various cities were refurbished, monuments erected, and pavilions built on the model of recent international exhibitions.

A yearlong series of events led to grandiose ceremonies in October and November of 1892 that involved the Spanish royal family and many foreign dignitaries. On October 9, Cánovas, his wife, and members of the royal family took part in a mock exploration off the Andalusian coast with escort ships from twelve foreign countries. At least twenty-four countries participated officially in the Spanish quadricentennial.

Replicas of Columbus’s boats sailed across the Atlantic. For a few weeks, Spain was at the center of the world. Parades in Madrid and Seville were echoed in Havana and Manila, and officials from the most powerful western countries paid homage to Spain.
zh: 西班牙为这场庆典花费了超过二百五十万比塞塔（pesetas）和四年的筹备。多座城市得到翻新，纪念碑竖立起来，展馆按照晚近国际博览会的样式建造。
一整年的系列活动通向1892年10月和11月的宏大典礼，西班牙王室成员和众多外国显贵参与其中。10月9日，卡诺瓦斯、他的夫人和王室成员在十二个外国派来的船只护航下，在安达卢西亚海岸外参加了一场模拟探险。至少有二十四个国家正式参加了西班牙的四百周年。
哥伦布船队的复制品横渡了大西洋。有几个星期，西班牙处于世界的中心。马德里和塞维利亚的游行在哈瓦那和马尼拉得到呼应，最强大的西方国家的官员向西班牙致敬。

en: The huge international participation was due, in a large part, to Cánovas’s careful packaging of both the celebration and its object, the discovery itself. He sold the quadricentennial not only as pageantry but as a challenge to the most enlightened minds, a yearlong symposium on past and present policy, on the role of Spain in the world, on Western civilization, and on the relevance of history. In a series of moves that anticipated the 1992 quincentennial, the quadricentennial junta set up a series of intellectual activities that legitimized the celebration.
zh: 庞大的国际参与，在很大程度上归功于卡诺瓦斯对庆典及其对象——发现本身——的精心包装。他推销四百周年，不只把它当作排场，还当作对最开明头脑的挑战，一场为期一年、关于过去与现在的政策、关于西班牙在世界上的角色、关于西方文明、关于历史何以与当下有关的研讨会。在一系列预示了1992年五百周年的举措中，四百周年委员会设立了一批为庆典赋予正当性的学术活动。

en: The junta created at least one serious academic journal, influenced others, dealt with learned societies, and commissioned research that still inspires European and American studies. From February 1891 to May 1892, more than fifty public lectures were delivered in the Ateneo de Madrid alone. Many titles show the role of the quadricentennial in shaping the categories and themes under which the conquest of the Americas is still discussed: the differential impact of various colonial systems on conquered populations, the accuracy of the Black Legend, the cultural legacies of pre-Conquest Americans, Spain’s treatment of Columbus, Columbus’s role as compared to that of other European explorers, his exact landing place, his exact burial place, etc.

These activities not only influenced participating academics, they also shaped the general public’s perception of what was at stake. First, they made the discovery and Columbus worthy of increased public attention by making them objects of learned discourse. Second, they gave anyone who granted that attention—individuals, parties, or states—an apparently neutral ground to celebrate in spite of conflicting connotations and purposes.
zh: 委员会至少创办了一份严肃的学术期刊，影响了其他期刊，与各学会打交道，并委托了至今仍在启发欧美研究的课题。从1891年2月到1892年5月，仅在马德里学术院（Ateneo de Madrid）就举办了五十多场公开讲座。许多题目显示出四百周年在塑造讨论美洲征服所用的范畴与主题方面的作用：不同殖民体系对被征服人口的不同影响，黑色传说（Black Legend）的准确性，前征服时代美洲原住民的文化遗产，西班牙对哥伦布的待遇，哥伦布与其他欧洲探险家的角色比较，他的确切登陆地点，他的确切埋葬地点，等等。
这些活动不仅影响了参与的学者，也塑造了公众对利害所在的认识。首先，它们把发现和哥伦布变成学术话语的对象，从而使他们值得更多的公众关注。其次，它们给任何给予这种关注的人——个人、政党或国家——提供了一块表面中立的场地，让他们尽管内涵与目的相互冲突仍能一同庆祝。

en: Connotations and purposes varied widely. Spanish urban crowds took the quadricentennial as the homage to Spain it was in part meant to be, the symbol of an impending revitalization. Journalist Angel Stor spoke in the name of many when he wrote: “There is in the discovery of America a character much greater than Isabella and Ferdinand the Catholic … much greater than Columbus himself, for never was an individual able to do what a people can. This character is Spain, the true protagonist of this wonderful epic.”
zh: 内涵与目的千差万别。西班牙的城市人群把四百周年当作它部分意图所在的对西班牙的致敬，当作一场即将到来的复兴的象征。记者安赫尔·斯托尔（Angel Stor）写道，道出了许多人的心声：“美洲的发现中有一个远比天主教君主伊莎贝拉和斐迪南更伟大的角色……远比哥伦布本人更伟大，因为个人从来做不到一个民族所能做到的事。这个角色就是西班牙，这部壮丽史诗的真正主角。”

en: Cánovas’s narrative was not too different from that of Stor. He saw in the celebration a unique occasion to reinforce Spain’s presence west of the Atlantic and—to a lesser extent—in Europe. But he also used the commemoration to consolidate his personal power. The quadricentennial made him a supporting character of Spain’s story, the necessary shadow of the protagonist. In a political context marked by Spain’s first experiment with “universal” (male) suffrage and nearly obsessional fears of losing face in Europe and elsewhere, Cánovas came out of the celebrations as a bona fide representative of the nation and a guarantor of her honor.
zh: 卡诺瓦斯的叙述与斯托尔的没有太大不同。他把庆典看作强化西班牙在大西洋以西——以及在较小程度上在欧洲——存在的独特机会。但他也利用纪念活动巩固个人权力。四百周年使他成了西班牙故事的配角，主角必要的影子。在一个以西班牙首次试验“普选”（男性）权、以及几乎无时无刻不担心在欧洲及其他地方丢脸为标志的政治语境中，卡诺瓦斯从庆典中走出来时，已是西班牙名副其实的代言人、维护国家荣誉的人。

en: Honor was not the only stake. To a large extent, Spain’s quadricentennial also aimed to create a space for a new conquest of the Americas. Although token gifts—such as schools and dispensaries—were made to the Philippines, the celebrants’ eyes were on the other side of the Atlantic. Many Spanish leaders felt the need to reinforce commercial and cultural ties with Latin America in the face of U.S. gains. At the same time, those who wanted Spanish olives or wine to enter the United States saw in the celebrations an occasion to establish contact with North American firms and agencies.
zh: 荣誉不是唯一的利害。在很大程度上，西班牙的四百周年还旨在为一次对美洲的新征服创造空间。虽然向菲律宾赠送了象征性的礼物——比如学校和诊疗所——庆祝者的眼睛却盯着大西洋彼岸。许多西班牙领袖感到，面对美国的进逼，有必要强化与拉丁美洲的商业和文化纽带。与此同时，那些想让西班牙橄榄或葡萄酒进入美国的人，把庆典看作与北美公司和机构建立联系的机会。

en: U.S. brokers, in turn, wanted contact but only on their own terms. Theirs was the only country whose name contained a continent (South Africa came much later), and whose imperial destiny was unfolding along manifest tracks. Thus if for Spain, the quadricentennial was an occasion to authenticate past splendors and imagine future glories, for many in the United States it was an opportunity to verify and celebrate their present course. Accordingly, U.S. officials paid lip service to Cánovas’s festivities, but invested their energy in
quadricentennial, the World’s Columbian Exposition of Chicago.
zh: 美国的掮客们反过来也想接触，但只按他们自己的条件。他们的国家是唯一一个国名里包含一个大洲的国家（南非要晚得多才出现），其帝国命运正沿着昭昭天命的轨道展开。因此，如果说对西班牙而言四百周年是认证往日辉煌、想象未来荣耀的机会，那么对许多美国人而言，它是核实并庆祝自己当前路线的机会。于是，美国官员对卡诺瓦斯的庆典只是口头敷衍，却把精力投入
四百周年——芝加哥世界哥伦布博览会（World’s Columbian Exposition）。

en: The Chicago Exposition actually opened in 1893, but by then, historical accuracy and even Columbus himself had become quite secondary. The intellectual aspect of the event barely mattered in spite of contributions from Harvard’s Peabody Museum and the Smithsonian Institution and the presence of then-rising star Franz Boas. Henry Adams later wrote in his

“The Exposition denied philosophy … [S]ince Noah’s Ark, no such Babel of loose and ill-jointed, such vague and ill-defined and unrelated thoughts and half-thoughts and experimental outcries … had ruffled the surface of the Lakes.”
zh: 芝加哥博览会实际上1893年才开幕，但到那时，历史的准确性、甚至哥伦布本人都已变得相当次要。尽管有哈佛皮博迪博物馆和史密森学会的贡献，以及当时崭露头角的弗朗茨·博厄斯（Franz Boas）的在场，这场活动的学术层面几乎无足轻重。亨利·亚当斯后来在他的
中写道：“博览会否定了哲学……自诺亚方舟以来，从未有过如此一座由松散而接合不良、模糊而界定不清、互不关联的思想、半截思想和试验性叫喊构成的巴别塔……搅皱五大湖的水面。”

en: Compared to Madrid 1892, Chicago 1893 was no intellectual event. The main point was money: to be spent and to be made. United States appropriations for the 1892 celebration in Madrid were a mere $25,000, thus one-tenth of U.S. appropriations for the 1889 fair in Paris and a trifle compared to the $5.8 million for the Chicago Exposition.

Paris 1889 and, closer to home, the 1876 centennial of U.S. independence in Philadelphia had proved to North American entrepreneurs that international fairs generated profits. By the late 1870s, consensus was reached among the likes of W. Rockefeller, C. Vanderbilt, J. P. Morgan, and W. Waldorf Astor that the United States needed one more of these money-making events. That it occurred in Chicago one year too late was the combined result of accidents and false starts among bureaucrats and investors. That it bore Columbus’s name and included a Spanish Infanta as the guest of honor were merely additional attractions.
zh: 与1892年的马德里相比，1893年的芝加哥不是一场学术活动。要点是钱：要花的钱和要赚的钱。美国为1892年马德里庆典的拨款仅2.5万美元，只有美国为1889年巴黎博览会拨款的十分之一，与芝加哥博览会的580万美元相比更是九牛一毛。
1889年的巴黎，以及更近在眼前的1876年费城美国独立百年纪念，已经向北美企业家证明国际博览会能生利。到1870年代末，W.洛克菲勒、C.范德比尔特、J.P.摩根和W.沃尔多夫·阿斯特之类的人物达成共识：美国需要再办一场这样的赚钱活动。它在芝加哥晚了一年才举行，是官僚和投资者之间种种意外与出师不利的共同结果。它冠以哥伦布之名、并请来一位西班牙王女（Infanta）作主宾，不过是额外的卖点。

en: Circumstantial as he was to his own occasion, Columbus gained a lot from Chicago. Commemorations feed on numbers and the 1893 quadricentennial was a display of the U.S. appetite for size: more participating countries, more acreage, more exhibits, more money than any fair the world had known. Chicago won the numbers game—second only to Paris for attendance—and provided Columbus his most successful celebration to date: $28.3 million in expenses; $28.8 million in receipts; 21.5 million people in attendance—and no protest in the local records. Some Spanish journalists ridiculed what they saw as a vulgar carnival, but the Chicago numbers spoke for themselves. Columbus was the wrapping for an extravagant Yankee bazaar; but in the end, the bazaar was so big that the wrapping was noticed.
zh: 尽管哥伦布对自己这场盛会而言只是个应景人物，他却从芝加哥获益良多。纪念活动以数字为食，而1893年的四百周年是一次对美国凡事求大的胃口的展示：参与国家更多、占地更广、展品更多、花钱更多，超过世界已知的任何博览会。芝加哥赢了数字游戏——参观人数仅次于巴黎——并为哥伦布提供了他迄今最成功的庆典：支出2830万美元；收入2880万美元；参观者2150万人次——而且地方记录中没有任何抗议。一些西班牙记者嘲笑他们眼中的粗俗嘉年华，但芝加哥的数字自己会说话。哥伦布是一场奢华扬基集市的包装纸；但到头来，集市大到让人注意到了包装纸。

en: Latin America certainly noticed. To be sure, Columbus’s metamorphosis into a Yankee hero, the lone ranger of the western seas, looked somewhat banal outside Chicago. Still, viewed from the far south, the fair belonged to a political and economic series from which it drew its symbolism. The Columbus story written in Chicago overlapped with the ongoing narrative of conquest that U.S. power was busily writing in the lands of this hemisphere. What was said to have happened in 1492 legitimized what was actually happening in the early 1890s. In 1889, Secretary of State James Gillepsie Blaine, one of the promoters of the celebration, had convened the first meeting of American states in Washington.

In 1890, Minor C. Keith acquired eight hundred thousand acres of public land in Costa Rica, the U.S. Congress passed the McKinley Tariff, and U.S. entrepreneurs controlled 80 percent of Cuban sugar exports. In 1891 U.S. admiral Bancroft Gherardi threatened to seize part of Haiti and the U.S. Navy prepared for war against Chile. In 1892, the postmaster of the United States, acting as a private citizen-broker, bought the entire foreign debt of the Dominican Republic. Four centuries after Spain, the United States was taking over. The path was the same: first the Caribbean, then the continental landmass. Columbus as Yankee looked somewhat more real, if not necessarily less foolish, in light of that ongoing expansion.
zh: 拉丁美洲当然注意到了。诚然，哥伦布变形为扬基英雄、西海独行侠，在芝加哥之外显得有点平庸。但从遥远的南方看去，这场博览会属于一个一连串政治与经济事件，象征意义正来自这些事件。在芝加哥写就的哥伦布故事，与美国权力正在这个半球的土地上忙于书写的征服叙述相重叠。被说成1492年发生的事，为1890年代初实际正在发生的事赋予了正当性。1889年，庆典的推动者之一、国务卿詹姆斯·吉莱斯皮·布莱恩（James Gillepsie Blaine）在华盛顿召集了美洲国家的第一次会议。

1890年，迈纳·C.基思（Minor C. Keith）在哥斯达黎加取得八十万英亩公有地，美国国会通过麦金莱关税（McKinley Tariff），美国企业家控制了古巴食糖出口的80%。1891年，美国海军将领班克罗夫特·杰拉迪（Bancroft Gherardi）威胁要夺取海地的一部分，美国海军准备对智利开战。1892年，美国邮政总长以私人公民兼掮客的身份，买下了多米尼加共和国的全部外债。西班牙之后四百年，美国正在接手。路径相同：先是加勒比，然后是大陆陆块。在那场持续扩张的映照下，作为扬基的哥伦布显得真实了一些——尽管未必少几分愚蠢。

en: Europe also noticed. The Pan-American strategy was designed in part to block European incursions in the hemisphere. In the 1880s, British investments in South America exceeded those of the United States. The French also were perceived as a threat until the 1889 collapse of their canal project. Even German and Italian ventures, relatively small, were watched with suspicion from North America. Thus, from 1890 to the end of the fair, Europeans were told repeatedly how to read Columbus and what this new reading meant for the hemisphere.
zh: 欧洲也注意到了。泛美战略的设计，部分就是为了阻挡欧洲对这个半球的渗透。1880年代，英国在南美的投资超过美国。法国人也被视为威胁，直到1889年他们的运河计划破产。甚至规模相对较小的德国和意大利冒险事业，也被北美方面以怀疑的目光盯着。因此，从1890年到博览会结束，欧洲人被反复告知该如何解读哥伦布，以及这种新解读对这个半球意味着什么。

en: The imposition of this new reading required the production of a number of silences. Since some traces could not be erased, their historical significance had to be reduced. They became inconsequential or significant only in light of the new interpretation. Thus, the official guide to the fair dismissed as meaningless the first 280 years of Euro-American history: the history of this hemisphere prior to 1776 was a mere “preparatory period” to the rise of the United States. The meaning of the discovery could be measured by the number of bushels of wheat that the United States now produced and the length of its railways. Shunning Europe and Latin America in the same stroke, the guide added: “Most fitting it is, therefore, that the people of the greatest nation on the continent discovered by Christopher Columbus, should lead in the celebration of the Four Hundredth Anniversary of that event.”
zh: 强加这种新解读，需要生产一批沉默。既然有些痕迹无法抹除，它们的历史意义就必须被削减。它们变得无关紧要，或只在新解释的映照下才有意义。于是，博览会的官方指南把欧洲人到达后美洲历史的头280年贬为无意义：1776年之前这个半球的历史，不过是美国崛起的“准备期”。发现的意义，可以用美国如今生产的小麦蒲式耳数和铁路里程来衡量。指南一笔甩开欧洲和拉丁美洲，补充道：“因此，由克里斯托弗·哥伦布所发现的大陆上最伟大国家的人民来领衔庆祝该事件四百周年，是再恰当不过的。”

en: Even U.S. citizens were told in unmistakable terms what Columbus was not about, lest working-class Irish and, especially, Italian families use him as a shield to hide their own highly suspect invasion. The number of immigrants from Europe had doubled between 1860 and 1893. At the same time, the countries of origins were increasingly non-English speaking areas of what passed then for “Southern Europe”: Italy, Russia, Poland, Bohemia, and other lands of doubtful whiteness. By 1890, the number of Italian immigrants was over three hundred thousand.
zh: 甚至美国公民也被明白无误地告知哪些事跟哥伦布沾不上边，以免工人阶级的爱尔兰家庭、尤其是意大利家庭拿他当盾牌，掩护他们自己那场在主流眼中极为可疑的“入侵”。1860年至1893年间，来自欧洲的移民数量翻了一番。与此同时，来源国越来越多是当时所谓“南欧”的非英语地区：意大利、俄国、波兰、波希米亚，以及其他白度存疑的土地。到1890年，意大利移民已超过三十万。

en: In the context of that migration, ideas suggesting the biological inferiority of the “southern” immigrants and the threat they constituted to the “future race” of the United States became widespread. Progressive journals taking the new immigrants’ side published articles with titles such as “Are the Italians a Dangerous Class?”

Two years after the number of Italians passed the three hundred thousand mark, railroad magnate Chauncey M. Depew, having conceded in a speech that Columbus Day belonged “not to America, but to the world,” went on to warn against “unhealthy immigration,” urging U.S. citizens to “quarantine against disease, pauperism and crime.”

It took only a centennial for similar propositions to reappear in California and Florida in the 1990s. But by then, the diatribes were directed at Mexican and Caribbean immigrants; the Italians and the Russians had been integrated in the white melting pot.
zh: 在那场移民的背景下，暗示“南方”移民生物学上的低劣、以及他们对美国“未来种族”构成威胁的观念广为流传。站在新移民一边的进步派期刊发表的文章，标题诸如《意大利人是一个危险的阶级吗？》。
意大利人数突破三十万大关两年后，铁路大亨昌西·M.迪普（Chauncey M. Depew）在一次演讲中先承认哥伦布日“不属于美国，而属于世界”，接着却警告要防范“不健康的移民”，敦促美国公民“对疾病、赤贫和犯罪实行隔离检疫”。
类似的论调只过了一个世纪，就在1990年代的加利福尼亚和佛罗里达重现。只是到那时，抨击的矛头指向墨西哥和加勒比移民；意大利人和俄国人已经被整合进白人的熔炉。

en: Vanity notwithstanding, those who wrote the script for Chicago could not control all the possible readings of that script. Their triumph was due, in part, to their taking Columbus further out of context than did their predecessors. Once that was done, however, Columbus was not theirs alone. Successful celebrations decontextualize successfully the events they celebrate, but in so doing they open the door to competitive readings of these events. The richer the ritual, the easier it is for subsequent performers to change parts of the script or to impose new interpretations. The recent controversies about the quincentennial celebrations of the Bahamas landing were possible in part because of the extravagant investments—both material and symbolic—of the celebrants. But the reach of these controversies was also increased by the significance of past celebrations. As rituals of a special kind, commemorations build upon each other, and each celebration raises the stake for the next one. Cánovas’s fiesta and the earlier parades of Italian- and Irish-Americans had unwittingly promoted the Chicago fair. The Chicago fair, in turn, was read by some immigrants as an acknowledgment of their presence in the melting pot—clearly an unexpected effect from the point of view of the magnates. From then on, Catholic Americans felt partly vindicated by their hero’s national recognition.
zh: 尽管自负，为芝加哥撰写脚本的人并不能控制这个脚本所有可能的读解。他们的胜利，部分归功于他们比前人把哥伦布带离语境更远。然而一旦如此，哥伦布就不再只属于他们。成功的庆典成功地把所庆祝的事件去语境化，但这样做也为对这些事件的竞争性读解打开了大门。仪式越丰盛，后来的表演者就越容易改动脚本的某些部分，或强加新的解释。晚近围绕巴哈马登陆五百周年庆典的争论之所以可能，部分正是因为庆祝者们奢华的投入——物质的和象征的。但这些争论的影响范围，也因过往庆典的意义而扩大。作为一种特殊仪式，纪念活动彼此叠加，每一场庆典都为下一场抬高赌注。卡诺瓦斯的盛典，以及更早的意大利裔和爱尔兰裔美国人的游行，无意中为芝加哥博览会做了推手。而芝加哥博览会反过来被一些移民读解为对他们存在于熔炉之中的承认——从大亨们的角度看，这显然是个意外效果。从那时起，美国天主教徒因其英雄获得全国承认而感到自己多少得到了正名。

en: By the 1890s, the appropriation of Columbus in the United States truly became a national phenomenon. Narratives were produced that rewrote a past meant to certify the inevitability of a Columbian connection. Ethnic and religious leaders, counties and munic palities started to look for traces of Columbus in their origins, silencing prior narratives, busily creating others. By the end of the decade, for instance, it had become public knowledge that the Ohio town of Columbus was named after the Discoverer. Yet the major documents that record the establishment of Columbus as seat of the state government of Ohio do not make any reference to the Genoese navigator. Columbus the man was not mentioned in the original bill, or in the

when the bill was signed and sent to the Senate. Nor was he mentioned when the bill was amended a few years later. In 1816, Governor Worthington, addressing the Ohio legislature, simply stated that Columbus had become the permanent seat of local government without mention of Columbus the man. In that same year,

did make an allusion to the United States as a “Columbian Republic,” but its descriptions of Columbus the town do not evoke the Genoese sailor. Nor do successive editions. Further descriptions or histories of both the town and the state from the 1830s to the 1850s are equally silent about a connection between Columbus, Ohio, and Columbus, the Genoese. Even a comprehensive history of the town published in 1873 does not mention such a connection.
In short, as late as 1873, the connection between Columbus, Ohio, and Christopher Columbus was historically irrelevant.
zh: 到了1890年代，把哥伦布写进自己的历史，在美国真正成了全国现象。人们生产出种种叙述，重写一段旨在证明哥伦布关联之必然性的过去。族群与宗教领袖、县和市镇开始在各自的起源中寻找哥伦布的痕迹，让先前的叙述沉默，忙于创造新的叙述。例如，到这个十年结束时，俄亥俄州的哥伦布市以发现者命名已成公共常识。然而，记录哥伦布被确立为俄亥俄州政府所在地的主要文献，对这位热那亚航海家只字未提。最初的法案没有提到哥伦布这个人，法案签署并送交参议院时的
也没有。几年后法案修订时同样没有提到他。1816年，沃辛顿（Worthington）州长向俄亥俄州议会致辞，只是说哥伦布已成为州政府的永久所在地，没有提及哥伦布这个人。同年，
确实把美国称为“哥伦布共和国”，但它对哥伦布市的描述并不唤起那位热那亚水手。后续各版也没有。1830年代到1850年代关于该市和该州的进一步描述或历史，同样对俄亥俄州哥伦布市与热那亚人哥伦布之间的关联保持沉默。甚至1873年出版的一部该市通史也没有提到这种关联。
简言之，直到1873年，俄亥俄州哥伦布市与克里斯托弗·哥伦布之间的关联在历史上仍是无关紧要的。

en: Yet by 1892, in the euphoria that surrounded the Chicago fair, historians were listing Columbus, Ohio, as an obvious proof of Columbus’s wide recognition in the United States.
A century later, for the launching of AmeriFlora ’92, a quincentennial event set in Columbus, President Bush reaffirmed the inevitability of a connection by then firmly established:
zh: 然而到1892年，在环绕芝加哥博览会的亢奋中，历史学家们已把俄亥俄州哥伦布市列为哥伦布在美国广受承认的明证。
一个世纪后，为启动设在哥伦布市的五百周年活动“92美洲花展”（AmeriFlora ’92），布什总统重申了那时已牢固确立的关联的必然性：

en: It is most fitting that this special event has been designated an official Quincentennial Project by the Jubilee Commission. To be held in Columbus, Ohio—the largest city in the world named after this great explorer—AmeriFlora ’92 will celebrate the rich cultural heritage of not only the lands he discovered but also the continent from which he travelled.
zh: 五百周年庆典委员会（Jubilee Commission）把这项特别活动指定为官方五百周年项目，是再恰当不过的。92美洲花展将在俄亥俄州哥伦布市——世界上以这位伟大探险家命名的最大城市——举行，它不仅将庆祝他所发现的土地的丰富文化遗产，也将庆祝他出发的那片大陆的丰富文化遗产。

en: The final measure of Chicago’s success is the extent to which it naturalized Columbus. A century after the fair, fourteen states other than Ohio had towns named Columbus, and a number of Columbias filled the U.S. landscape.

Yet President Bush’s reference to the cultural heritage of American Indians aside, this more American Columbus was also a whiter Columbus. All hyphens are not equal in the pot that does not melt. The second part of the compound—Irish-
, Jewish-
, Anglo-
—always emphasizes whiteness. The first part only measures compatibility with the second at a given historical moment.

Thus, as he became more American, Columbus had to become whiter, in spite of the anti-Italian racism prevailing at the time of the Chicago fair. As Columbus became whiter he also contributed to the whitening of the people who claimed him as part of their past, further opening to multiple interpretations the narrative officialized at Chicago. The very success of the fair created an ideological breach in the vision of the United States proposed by some of its promoters.
zh: 衡量芝加哥成功的最终尺度，是它把哥伦布归化到什么程度。博览会一个世纪后，除俄亥俄外还有十四个州有以哥伦布命名的城镇，一批哥伦比亚（Columbia）填满了美国的地景。
然而，撇开布什总统对美洲印第安人文化遗产的提及不谈，这个更美国的哥伦布也是一个更白的哥伦布。在这个并未熔成一体的“熔炉”里，并非所有连字符都平等。复合词的后半部分——爱尔兰裔-
、犹太裔-
、盎格鲁-
——总是强调白人属性。前半部分只衡量在特定历史时刻与后半部分的兼容程度。
因此，随着他变得更美国，哥伦布不得不变得更白，尽管芝加哥博览会之时反意大利的种族主义正盛行。随着哥伦布变得更白，他也使那些把他纳入自身过去的人更容易被归入白人，从而进一步把在芝加哥被官方化的叙述向多重解释敞开。博览会的成功本身，在其某些推动者提出的美国愿景中撕开了一道意识形态缺口。

en: Three years after the fair, determined to muddle the script broadcast in Chicago, Italians in New York founded the Sons of Columbus Legion, which celebrated Columbus Day the following year.

Their efforts mingled with those of the Irish, though not always by way of formal collaboration. The Knights, in particular, worked hard for their chosen ancestor. As Irish-Americans spread through the country with the full benefits of white status, the Knights petitioned successive state legislatures to make October 12 a legal holiday. By 1912, they were victorious. Columbus himself, further out of the context of 1492 Europe, became more Irish than ever—until Italian-Americans made new gains in the continuing contest for racial and historical legitimacy with the mass migrations that followed each of two world wars.
zh: 博览会三年后，纽约的意大利人决意搅乱芝加哥广播的脚本，创立了哥伦布之子军团（Sons of Columbus Legion），次年庆祝了哥伦布日。

他们的努力与爱尔兰人的努力交融，尽管并不总是通过正式合作。尤其是骑士团，为他们选定的祖先卖力工作。随着爱尔兰裔美国人带着白人身份的全部好处在全国散开，骑士团先后向各州议会请愿，要求把10月12日定为法定假日。到1912年，他们胜利了。哥伦布本人愈发脱离1492年欧洲的语境，变得比以往任何时候都更爱尔兰——直到意大利裔美国人在两次世界大战后接踵而至的大移民中，在这场争夺种族与历史正当性的持续竞赛里取得新的进展。

en: Latin Americans also appropriated Columbus in unexpected ways, skewing plans made in both Madrid and Washington. The Spanish government had promoted emigration to South America in the late nineteenth century, as part of a larger movement to promote

in the region. From Madrid’s viewpoint, attachment to Spanish culture and veneration of a Spanish heritage would counteract the growing political and economic influence of the United States. Madrid’s promotion of Columbus Day as the day of Hispanity in the colonies and former colonies fitted well into this scheme, which was in obvious conflict with the dominant image of Columbus promoted in the United States. Latin Americans, who participated in both quadricentennials, resolved these conflicts in their own favor.
zh: 拉丁美洲人也以出人意料的方式把哥伦布写进自己的历史，打乱了马德里和华盛顿双方的计划。西班牙政府在十九世纪末推动向南美移民，作为在该地区推广
的更大运动的一部分。从马德里的观点看，对西班牙文化的依恋和对西班牙遗产的尊崇，将抵消美国日益增长的政治和经济影响。马德里在殖民地和前殖民地推动把哥伦布日作为西班牙性之日（day of Hispanity），很契合这个盘算，而它与在美国推广的哥伦布主导形象明显冲突。参加了两场四百周年的拉丁美洲人，把这些冲突解决得对自己有利。

en: The image of Columbus with a cowboy hat escorting Wells Fargo wagons was simply not convincing south of Texas, but it did challenge the Columbus as Renaissance monk favored by Cánovas’s Spain. In trying to make of Columbus a North American, the Chicago fair made of him a man of the Americas. That was due to a confusion of tongues, deliberate only in part. From the U.S. viewpoint, turning the discoverer into an “American” was equivalent to putting on him a “made in USA” label, for the United States
America.

Latin Americans, for their part, could not appropriate Columbus from Spain. Their cultural heritage, their views on blending, their semiperipheral position in the world economy simply did not lead to this take-over: they had neither the means nor the will. Thus, they had watched from the sidelines the Americanization of Columbus. But that Americanization had different implications for the Latin Americans. For them, the hemisphere is not the exclusive property of

“American” means neither “gringo” nor “Yankee”—at least not necessarily. An “American” Columbus belonged to the hemisphere. Adding their own line to two different scripts, Latin Americans forced both the Spanish and the U.S. figures into their “blending” discourse. Throughout Latin America, October 12 became either the day to honor Spanish influence or to honor its opposite or, more often, to celebrate a blending of the two: Discovery Day, the Day of the Americas, or simply
, the Day of the Race, the day of the people—a day for ourselves, however defined, for ethnicity however constructed.
has in Merida or Cartagena accents unknown in San Juan or in Santiago de Chile, and Columbus wears a different hat in each of these places.
zh: 头戴牛仔帽、护送富国银行（Wells Fargo）马车的哥伦布形象，在得克萨斯以南根本说服不了人，但它确实挑战了卡诺瓦斯的西班牙所青睐的作为文艺复兴修士的哥伦布。在试图把哥伦布变成北美人的过程中，芝加哥博览会把他变成了美洲人。这源于一场语言的混淆，而其中只有一部分是刻意的。从美国的观点看，把发现者变成“美国人”（American）等于给他贴上“美国制造”的标签，因为在他们看来，America
美国。
拉丁美洲人这边，则无法从西班牙那里占用哥伦布。他们的文化遗产、他们关于融合的看法、他们在世界经济中的半边缘位置，根本不会导向这种接管：他们既无手段也无意愿。因此，他们曾从场边旁观哥伦布的美国化。但那种美国化对拉丁美洲人有不同的含义。对他们来说，这个半球不是
的独家财产。American 未必指“美国佬”（gringo）或“扬基”。把哥伦布称作“美洲人”（American），就是把他看作整个美洲的人。拉丁美洲人在两个不同的脚本里加上自己的台词，把西班牙和美国的人物都强行纳入他们的“融合”话语。在整个拉丁美洲，10月12日要么成了纪念西班牙影响的日子，要么成了纪念其对立面的日子，更常见的是庆祝两者融合的日子：发现日、美洲日，或干脆叫

children: 种族日（El Día de la Raza）

zh: ，种族之日，人民之日——一个属于我们自己的日子，无论我们如何定义，无论族群性如何建构。
在梅里达或卡塔赫纳的口音，是圣胡安或智利圣地亚哥所没有的，而哥伦布在这些地方各戴一顶不同的帽子。
